  My sister and I were pressured to gain as much weight as possible every hour of our lives, and we were grounded for a week each time we did not finish all the food on our plates (which had 3 or 4 servings of every item.) I was grounded nearly my entire childhood. My sister...   Suddenly my sister hated me, and my parents praised her for it. Soon it was "If you don't finish your plate, you do all the chores in the house for a week." Guess who did every chore in the house until I was 18? I had to cook, clean, mow the lawn, pull weeds, take care of the pets... And I had to watch them suck down food every 10 minutes of every day, complaining to me that they need more, or that I didn't season it properly, or that I intentionally undercooked it to mess with them.

  When I wasn't doing chores, I refused to study the bible, which meant I was put in my room with nothing but my bed and dresser for entire weekends while they ordered pizza. I was obviously depressed, so my parents took me to a therapist.

  The therapist seemed like a nice guy, and I explained to them that my parents never do anything and that I was tired of doing everything for them. I was becoming suicidal at this point, around age 15. Little did I know, the therapist was telling my parents everything I said, seeing as how I was a minor, and after the first appointment, my father finished his third dinner, actually took the plate to the kitchen, and yelled at me, saying, "Don't ever say I don't do anything around here!" and he threw the plate into the sink, of course breaking it. After that, I'd refused to see the therapist from then on.

  My parents asked the pastor of our church to speak with me privately instead, and he explained to me that I had to respect my parents, as per God's orders. I pleaded with him, explaining how I was used as a slave and told how worthless I am daily, but he wouldn't budge. I told him I didn't believe in God in the first place, and wouldn't you know it, he told my parents. Now, I understand spanking a child isn't necessarily abuse, not in most cases even, but I don't hesitate to say that my parents beat me for not being religious. They would wear spoons out, leaving small splinters in my skin, with welts. So I pretended to be religious until I turned 18. By that time, they had gained more weight, each of them weighing around 400 pounds. At this moment, my sister is 5'4" and I believe, based on what she posts on Facebook that she's about 250 to 300.

  I went to university, working odd jobs and trying to get by, but I buckled. I buckled hard. I locked myself in my dorm room starving myself, sleeping 20 hours at a time, and having crying spells. Several friends reported that they hadn't seen me in over a week to the campus police, so they came into my room and got me to the nearby hospital. My parents called, and actually sounded upset and worried. I was a fucking idiot. I fucking bought it.  

I actually believed they could possibly change. I went back home that Summer, and of course, obeasts never change. Not on their own. They immediately ridiculed everything about me. They explained that they were extremely disappointed with me because I didn't call them, that I don't love them. They asked me to clean their kitchen and I just went into a daze, half conscious. I cleaned the kitchen, vacuumed the house, and went downstairs to the basement (where my room was) and took copious amounts of sleeping pills, pain pills, benadryl, washed it down with a fifth of vodka.

  Obviously I didn't die, which upset me more than anything, even my worthless family, when I woke up in the hospital. I was there for 4 days after, and spent a month in the psychiatrist building next door. My parents asked me to go home with them when I got out...

  I had to accept it. They're just bad, and will never be human. They are the worst fucking things on this planet and while I consider myself a calm and polite person in 99% of my life, if I see them again, I will put a stake through each one of their heads.
